# `property-added-required`

New required property

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `error` in requests, `info` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `property-added-required` (both directions), `property-added-required-in-request`, `property-added-required-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A new required property in an object schema.

## Why this default

In requests: old clients don't send it and are rejected. In responses: clients receive an extra field, which they ignore.

## Example

From test case [`property-added-required`](../../test/cases/property-added-required/): A new required property in a request body.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          name:
            type: string
+         age:
+           type: integer
+       required:
+       - age
```

Findings:

- `property-added-required-in-request` · error · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). See [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  property-added-required: info
```

## How to fix

In requests, make the property optional with a server-side default.
